$\therefore$ $x<2$

The straight line y=kx+b slopes upward to the right, and intersects the x-axis at x=-4 on the x-axis; from the figure, it is above the x-axis to the right of x=-4. The other straight line y=mx+n slopes downward to the right, and intersects the x-axis at x=2 on the x-axis; from the figure, it is above the x-axis to the left of x=2.
Reasoning: The inequality kx+b>0 means that the function value of the straight line y=kx+b is greater than 0, that is, the image is above the x-axis, therefore from the figure we get x>-4. The inequality mx+n>0 means that the function value of the straight line y=mx+n is greater than 0, that is, the image is above the x-axis, therefore from the figure we get x<2. When the two conditions hold simultaneously, take the intersection, obtaining -4<x<2.
